subject: Hosted API upgrade: proposed commit increase + rate/readjustment
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbit.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T14:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal + commit increase question

Hannah,

Thanks again for the call earlier today — Orbit is preparing for a new product launch in Q3 and our forecasts are showing sustained higher usage. Right now we're on the hosted plan with a 500M token monthly commit. We're looking at a conservative upgrade to a 1.2B monthly commit, with potential step-ups if traffic continues to grow.

Two quick asks to help us finalize forecasts for procurement:
- Can Redwood confirm the effective unit rate for a 1.2B commit (tokens/month) vs our current band?
- We need clarity on rate limits and soft-throttle behavior — during launches we have short spikes. Will you route to a higher soft limit or add burst capacity?

I've attached a usage extract for April and a short launch model. Happy to jump on a quick call this week to align.

Thanks,
Sarah Lin
Director of Platform
Orbit AI

(attachment: orbit-usage-report-apr.pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbit.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + commit increase question

Hi Sarah — thanks for the note and the stats, this is helpful.

Short answers up front:
- Pricing: we can put together a 12-month commitment for 1.2B/month with a stepped unit discount compared to your current band. I'll have Karthik share a concrete quote.
- Rate limits / spikes: Redwood supports burst capacity and can route traffic to a dedicated pool for launches; we also have prefix/KV caching that often smooths token volume for repetitive prompts. If you expect sustained spikes (minutes-hours), we recommend a short burst add-on + a canary window to validate latency.

Next steps I propose: Karthik will draft a playbook (commit tiers, rate limits, canary window, burst band) and a pricing worksheet. If you confirm the 1.2B intent, we can prepare a signature-ready DocuSign and a mutual action plan.

Looping in Karthik — can you share a draft pricing sheet and an ops checklist for the launch?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:23:00Z
Subject: Orbit AI - internal: pricing & ops recommendation

Team — Orbit (DEAL-67842) is ready to move from 500M -> 1.2B tokens/month. Sarah asked specifically about unit pricing and rate-limit behavior for launch spikes. Key constraints: launch expected mid-August, short windows of high QPS for a few hours, then sustained uplift over months.

Please advise on the following by end of day Thursday:
1) Recommended list price / unit rate for 1.2B commit (12-month term). Include any onboarding credit we can offer to close.
2) Ops: can we enable a temporary dedicated pool + burst cushion (they prefer not to go fully Dedicated) and what are the latency SLOs?
3) Contract: any redlines on data retention / audit logs for Orbit? They are security-conscious.

I'll prep the mutual action plan and put the DocuSign template behind it once we have pricing.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Orbit AI - internal: pricing & ops recommendation

Quick draft from pricing side:
- 12-month term, 1.2B tokens/month commit (annualized). Effective unit price = $0.00028 per token for committed volume (tiered).
- We can offer a 10% one-time onboarding credit applied to month 1 invoice to help with migration costs.
- Burst cushion: add a 20% short-window burst band (billed on overage) with automatic soft-fallback to orbit-specific compatible model if the burst exhausts the cushion.
- Ops posture: enable a temporary dedicated pool during the 72-hour launch window (can be scheduled) — latency SLO during that window: p95 <= 220ms (text-gen); p99 <= 450ms. Outside the window they stay on Hosted with KV caching enabled.

Attached is pricing-sheet-v4.xlsx with the detailed numbers and two alternative step-up ladders (month-6 increase to 1.5B, or flat 1.2B).

My recommendation: propose the flat 1.2B with the 20% burst add-on and the 10% onboarding credit. Make DocuSign for the 12-month commit and include the step-up path as an amendment.

Karthik
Director, Revenue — Redwood

From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@orbit.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Finance <finance@orbit.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API upgrade: proposed commit increase + rate/readjustment

Thanks — this is clear and close to what we had in mind. Orbit is comfortable with the 12-month 1.2B commit and the burst cushion approach. Two confirmations from finance:
- We'll sign the DocuSign for the 12-month commitment with the 10% onboarding credit applied to our first invoice.
- Please include the optional month-6 ladder to 1.5B as Amendment A (we may elect it later).

Please send the signature packet and the mutual action plan; I've CC'd our finance contact who will be the signer.

On the ops side, we'll schedule the 72-hour dedicated window in August once we get the DocuSign complete. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sarah Lin
Director of Platform, Orbit AI
